This section outlines how we value coastal protection as an ecosystem service within the GEP
framework. Coastal habitats reduce the energy of waves and storm surge before it reaches the
shore, so property and infrastructure behind them suffer less damage than they would on a bare
coast. The service is therefore valued as avoided storm and flood damage, and it is reported for
two habitats: mangroves and coral reefs. Both are attributed to the country whose coast they
protect, and the two components are added to give one national coastal protection value.
Mangroves and coral reefs are not the only habitats that protect coasts, so the value covers these
two habitats only, and each country's row states which of the two its total includes.

## Source

The write-up is `Coastal_Protection.docx` (28 October 2026) in the shared folder of current
write-ups. The registered author code is the six files at commit `7ea35e798`. The mangrove values
are the World Bank wealth-accounts package's 2019 values, and the coral values are Beck et al.
(2018) in 2011 dollars.


## Quantity

Neither component is modelled from habitat extent inside this module. Both arrive as published
per-country tables in which the physical protection modelling has already been done upstream, so
the quantity stage here is the read and the aggregation onto the country list rather than a
biophysical calculation.

**Mangroves.** The mangrove component is the World Bank Changing Wealth of Nations mangrove
table, staged as `data_mangroves_2019.xlsx`. It carries, per country, the mangrove area in
hectares, a protection value per hectare, and the annual protection value that is their product,
all for 2019 and all in current US dollars. The table matches the CWoN 2024 package's outputs for
2019 exactly (`mangroves_unit_value_cd.dta` and `mangroves_annual_cd.dta`, 151 countries). The
model computes the value as area times value per hectare, which reproduces the published annual
value to within 2e-7 in total and 0.024% for any one country (the rate is rounded in the table). Because the table is keyed on the r264 country label, a country that the
correspondence splits into sub-regions arrives as several rows, and those rows are summed so that
each country ends up with exactly one value.

**Countries the mangrove source excluded.** The World Bank's mangrove analysis removed six
countries for a bug in its geospatial analysis: Guinea-Bissau, the Democratic Republic of the
Congo, Egypt, Hong Kong, Iran, and Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (*Building Coastal Resilience
with Mangroves*, 2024, Appendix 1, Data Cleaning items 3 and 4). The package's processing writes
zero area for every country absent from its source, so the table shows these six at zero. Their
mangrove component is published as missing, not zero, from the staged list
`mangrove_excluded_geospatial_errors.csv`. Egypt and Iran keep their coral value, labelled coral
protection only. The other four have no component and no value. The same appendix also removed 18
countries holding under 100 ha of mangroves. Seventeen of them publish a zero mangrove component,
and Anguilla is missing because neither table carries it. Whether to treat those zeros as
unestimated is an open decision.

**Coral reefs.** The coral component is the annual expected flood protection benefit table
staged as `coral_reefs_annual_expected_benefit_nfamara.xlsx`, which gives one annual benefit per
country in 2011 US dollars. This table is keyed on country name rather than country code, so it
is joined to the correspondence on the name and then reduced to one row per country before the
currency conversion below.

## Price

No price is applied in this module. Both source tables are already monetary, which means the
quantity and price stages are fused upstream and the attribution factor is one:

$$
\text{GEP}_{\text{coastal protection}} = Q \cdot P \cdot \lambda = \text{avoided damage} \times 1 \times 1
$$

The only monetary adjustment made here is a currency year alignment. The mangrove table is
already in the base year's dollars and needs none. The coral table is in 2011 US dollars, so
every value is multiplied by one scalar: the US CPI annual-mean ratio between 2019 and 2011
(FRED's CPIAUCSL, the shared US CPI series in `utilities.usd_deflation_factor`), which is 1.1366
on the staged data. The values are dollars, not local currency, so one US factor
carries every country. A per-country inflation rate would answer a different question.

## Valuation

The two components are joined on country and year, and the national value is the sum of the
components that are measured. A component a table does not carry stays missing rather than zero.
The coral table lists 80 countries and leaves out some that have reefs, Japan among them, so a
country's absence from a table is not evidence that the habitat gives no protection there. A
zero the source table reports, such as zero mapped mangrove area, stays zero.

Each row carries a coverage label, `coastal_protection_coverage`, naming what its total covers:
mangrove and coral protection, coral protection only, or mangrove protection only. The coastal
group decided that where coral protection is valued and the mangrove estimate is missing, the coral
value stands and the row reads coral protection only. Because other habitats also protect coasts,
a row with both components is still not all of nature's coastal protection, so the label states
which of the two modelled components the total includes, not that the total is complete. A
component measured on only some of a split country's sub-regions is called partial in the label.
No country is in that shape on the staged data. Where neither component is measured, the label is
missing along with the value.

$$
\text{GEP}_{\text{coastal protection},c} = V^{\text{mangrove}}_{c,2019} + V^{\text{coral}}_{c,2011} \cdot D_{2011 \rightarrow 2019}
$$

where $V^{\text{mangrove}}_{c,2019}$ is the country's annual mangrove protection value in 2019
dollars, $V^{\text{coral}}_{c,2011}$ is its annual coral reef protection benefit in 2011 dollars,
and $D_{2011 \rightarrow 2019}$ is the US CPI factor between those years. The result is
written as one row per country for the base year 2019, with the two components kept as separate
columns beside the total so that either can be inspected on its own.

On the currently staged input data this gives a known-component total of $36.28$ billion in 2019
US dollars, of which $30.40$ billion is the mangrove component and $5.88$ billion is the coral reef
component. The 46 countries with both components measured sum to $32.68$ billion.

## Known limitations

Two properties of the calculation are worth stating because they affect coverage rather than
arithmetic, and neither is silent once you know to look for it.

The coral table is joined on country name, not on a code. A name that the correspondence spells
differently would drop the country without failing, so the join is a place to check first when a
coastal country is missing.

Because the module consumes pre-valued national tables, it cannot separate the physical extent of
a habitat from the value assigned to it. A change in either the mapped habitat area or the damage
function behind these tables enters here only as a changed national total.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory, holding the
r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, `coastal_protection_gep` (the known-component total),
`coastal_protection_gep_mangrove`, `coastal_protection_gep_coral_reef`,
`coastal_protection_gep_both_components` (the total where both components are measured) and
`coastal_protection_coverage` (the coverage label). The same columns are in
`gep_by_country_base_year.gpkg` beside it, which carries the country boundaries for the map.

## Coverage

The published table is one row for each of the account's 250 countries, base year 2019, in 2019
USD.

| Column | Positive | Zero | Missing | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Known-component total | 106 | 111 | 33 | \$36,282,030,656.66 |
| Mangrove | 63 | 120 | 67 | \$30,400,077,269.61 |
| Coral reef | 80 | 0 | 170 | \$5,881,953,387.05 |
| Both components measured | 46 | 0 | 204 | \$32,678,157,914.16 |

| Coverage label | Countries |
| --- | --- |
| mangrove and coral protection | 46 |
| coral protection only | 34 |
| mangrove protection only | 137 |
| missing (no component measured) | 33 |

Remaining zeros are carried from the source mangrove table, which records zero area for 120
countries. They include the 17 small-mangrove exclusions, whose interpretation remains open. For
111 of the 120 the coral table has no row, so their total is zero and reads mangrove protection
only. That includes landlocked and temperate countries such as Austria and the Netherlands, where
the label reflects which tables list the country rather than any coral value. A missing value
means the data to compute it is absent.

## Reproduction

An independent rebuild of all 250 rows from the two author tables, the country correspondence,
the CPI factor 1.13662268124 and the six exclusions matched the published totals and components
within a relative 1.2e-7, with identical missing values. That rebuild predates the coverage label.
The label change moved no measured value: all 250 totals and every measured component are
identical, and only the 145 zeros previously set for a component a table does not carry (8
mangrove, 137 coral) are now missing. The upstream habitat models are not rerun.

## What is open

- The small-mangrove zeros. Whether the 17 countries the mangrove source removed for holding
  under 100 ha stand as zeros or count as unestimated is the coastal group's decision on missing
  habitat data.
- The CPI series. The write-up cites the BLS CPI-U, and the library uses FRED's seasonally
  adjusted CPIAUCSL. The difference in the annual-mean ratio is not quantified.
